subject: Renewal & consolidation: Amplitude + Segment — pricing / retention trade-offs
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <mgomez@amplitude.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@segment.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal & consolidation: Amplitude + Segment — quick kickoff

Hi Maria / Tom —

We’re starting the renewal cycle for product analytics and API analytics. Current state: we use Segment for API/event routing and Amplitude for product analytics; both contracts come up in Q2. Given our push to simplify vendor plumbing and reduce duplicate per-event charges, leadership asked us to explore a consolidation approach (either move more routing into Segment or negotiate a combined commercial package with Amplitude).

High level asks from my side:
- Pricing sensitivity and available multi-product bundle discounts for our profile (annual commit, ~1.2B monthly events across environments).
- Retention / export SLAs: we rely on 13 months of raw event retention for long-tail analysis and compliance exports. Need clear limits and egress costs.
- Any additional setup/engineering fees for moving downstream connectors.

I attached a usage summary (redwood_usage_summary_q4-q1.csv) — it’s a high-level slice. Could you share preliminary position / ballpark by EOM? We’d like to set a procurement sync for week of Feb 22.

Thanks — Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_usage_summary_q4-q1.csv (csv))

From: Maria Gomez <mgomez@amplitude.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@amplitude.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal & consolidation: Amplitude + Segment — quick kickoff

Sergio —

Appreciate the context and usage snapshot. Quick responses inline:
- Discounting: We can offer a multi-product discount when Amplitude and Segment (Twilio Segment) are purchased through a joint commercial arrangement. Ballpark before legal review: 12–18% off list for a 12-month committed agreement at your scale, with step-up for a 24-month commit.
- Retention & exports: Standard Amplitude enterprise retention is 13 months for events; longer retention can be negotiated but incurs storage uplift. Exports to S3 are supported; egress is charged at tiered rates (I can share a modeled estimate if you give me expected monthly export volume).
- Engineering fees: There shouldn’t be mandatory migration fees for ingesting via Segment, but advanced pipeline work (e.g., transformation across workspaces) may be scoped as professional services.

I’ve attached a preliminary pricing workbook (renewal-pricing.xlsx) and a DocuSign for a short-term extension option if you need time to conclude negotiations.

Proposed next step: 30–45 minute alignment call this week with your procurement and product analytics leads to walk the workbook. Suggestions: Feb 23 at 11am PT or Feb 24 at 9am PT. Which works?

Best,
Maria Gomez
Account Executive — Amplitude
(Attachment: renewal-pricing.xlsx (xlsx))

From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@segment.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 07:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal & consolidation: Amplitude + Segment — quick kickoff

Sergio / Laura —

Happy to join the conversation. A few points from Segment’s side to consider:
- If you push more routing to Segment (source-side enrichment, fewer downstream transformations), that can reduce downstream Amplitude ingestion cost but will increase Segment compute/ingest cost. We can model net TCO given the usage file.
- We support 13 months retention by default but we charge for additional storage if you want hot retention beyond that in Segment’s CDP layer.
- We’ve run consolidation projects before; typically there’s a 2–6 week engineering window depending on how many transforms and destinations you have.

I’m available Feb 24 at 9am PT (fits Maria’s window). Will bring our solution architect.

— Tom

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <mgomez@amplitude.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@segment.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal & consolidation: Amplitude + Segment — quick kickoff

Thanks both — meeting confirmed for Feb 24, 9am PT. Agenda I’ll run:
1) Quick product/usage overview (5m) — Marissa
2) Commercial ask: target % discount and preferred contract length (5m) — Sergio
3) Retention/export requirements and egress modeling (10m) — Karthik
4) Migration/ops risks and timing (10m) — Marissa/Tom
5) Next steps / procurement timeline (5m) — Laura

Pre-reads: I uploaded a 90s summary of our export pattern and the big ticket destinations to the shared spreadsheet (link sent below). Maria — can you confirm the assumptions you used in the pricing workbook around our monthly export GB? Also, if Amplitude has any limitations on event schema transformations that would affect our connector design, flag those now so we can scope engineering work.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2027 15:44:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal & consolidation: Amplitude + Segment — quick kickoff

Quick internal recap after today’s call — please treat as action list: 

1) Commercial: Maria committed to an initial 12–15% bundle discount for a 12-month commit; terms TBD from legal. Maria to run a modeled capex/opex comparison after we confirm export volume assumptions. (Owner: Sergio / procurement)
2) Retention: Amplitude confirmed 13mo standard; extra retention will be block-priced. Karthik to validate how much long-tail export (GB/month) we need to keep in cold storage and estimate egress. (Owner: Karthik)
3) Engineering: Marissa to scope migration work (2–6 weeks) and estimate engineering FTEs and downtime windows; include connector and schema-mapping tasks.
4) Procurement timeline: Laura to target final commercial signoff by Mar 19 to avoid auto-renewal penalties.

Attachments: I saved the pricing workbook and the usage snapshot in the shared folder. We may need a short extension if legal requires contract language changes — Maria offered a 30-day short-term extension DocuSign to keep lanes open.

Next internal sync: Monday Feb 29 (I know leap day—this is our aggressive cadence) at 10am PT to review Karthik’s export numbers and Marissa’s engineering estimate. If those look good, Laura will push for procurement approval and we’ll route the draft to legal.

Thanks — Sergio
